decisions.issues: The ear is fixed. Nagoji's ear is now a tiny gold stud flush on the lobe with nothing hanging. His chin is clean-shaven, his sleeves reach his wrists, and his boots are visible. Small deviations remain: Nagoji rides level with Padmini on her right (viewer's left) instead of a little behind her on her left, Padmini's side-saddle seat cannot be confirmed, and her strapped walking stick is not visible. Ibrahim is correct: white turban, teal coat, pocketed vest, grey-flecked beard and the scar on his left cheek. Both Nair relatives are correct: bare-chested, white mundu, topknots. The sky is pre-dawn grey and the gate is behind the party. There is no text, and the open sky across the upper centre and right gives clean room for the caption.

v03 makes the requested fixes: the two Nair relatives ride behind (bare-chested, white mundu, hair knotted high, no turbans), Padmini's walking stick is strapped along the saddle with a sheathed sword at her right side, and Nagoji is in commander dress with boots (correct for page 1), a thick curled moustache and a clean chin. The beat holds: mist-lifting hills, a lotus channel, the shrine tree with cloth bundles and oil lamps, women with baskets, and children racing along the bund in the foreground. There is no painted text, and the misty sky at upper left and the water at the bottom give clean space for the caption. Remaining faults to list for the author: (1) Nagoji's ear stud has a tiny gold bead hanging just below the lobe, only a few pixels across and barely visible at print size; (2) the riders are mid-ground rather than truly small in the middle distance; (3) Padmini's face reads younger than fifties with a lined face; (4) Ibrahim's left-ear-to-jaw scar is not readable at this scale. v01 and v02 leave out the Nair relatives and show Padmini holding the stick in her hand, so v03 is the least flawed.

Hard checks all pass. Nagoji's ear ornament is a gold stud sitting flush on the lobe with nothing hanging. He has the thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, sleeves down to the wrists, boots, talwar, rust-red turban and broad red sash. Padmini's hair is thick and black, with a lined face, gold at throat and wrists, and a leather-wrapped sword hilt. She faces forward and does not turn her head. The setting is Kerala, with no text. Minor, not blocking: they ride past a whitewashed gateway with an iron-barred gate leaf at the right edge, which does not match the dark stone gate of 1.1. Her sword sits at the front of her left hip rather than her right side. The light is bright midday, after 1.2's morning mist, which reads as the ride being compressed. There is clear sky between and above the two heads for one Padmini balloon and two Nagoji balloons.

The fix is done. Padmini is still mounted and alone, in profile, chin lifted toward the road with the faintest smile. There is no guard and no gate. She matches her sheet: lined face, thick black hair coiled at the nape (a few grey highlight strands, as on the sheet), gold ball earring, gold bead necklace and bangle, cream-and-gold sari over her left shoulder with the right shoulder bare, and the leather-wrapped sword hilt at her right hip. Her hand on the reins is sound. Her brown horse with the white blaze matches 1.1. The walking stick is out of frame, which is acceptable. The bright daylight follows on from the morning in 1.2. A large empty sky at upper right holds both balloons clear of her face.

Acceptable. A low red laterite wall circles tiled Kerala roofs and broad trees, with no towers or bastions. The gate stands wide open and is broad enough for carts. Two bare-chested Nair guards with high topknots, no turbans, white mundu at about knee length, spears and small round shields watch toward the viewer. No riders are in frame. There is no fort, no European building and no text, and the brass standing lamps on the verandah are traditional. Minor: the mundu hang just to the knee rather than visibly hitched, and the light is bright midday like 1.3 and 1.4. Clear blue sky top left of centre has room for the caption.

v02 fixes all three required points. Nagoji's ear has a tiny round gold stud sitting flush on the lobe with nothing hanging. The gate guards are bare-headed Nair men with topknots, bare chests, white mundu, spears and round shields. Padmini's long stick is strapped along the saddle. Nothing else breaks. Nagoji matches the commander sheet: rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrists, red sash over the shoulder, period wrapped riding boots, talwar, and a thick moustache with a clean chin. Only at 4x zoom is there a faint grey shadow on the chin. Padmini matches her sheet (lined face, black curly hair coiled at the nape, cream and gold Kerala drape with no blouse, gold ball earrings and necklace). The horses and setting match 1.3, 1.5 and 2.2. Minor, non-blocking: Padmini's sword hilt shows at her left hip rather than her right. The guard's topknot sits at the crown, not the front, and his mundu hangs below the knee. The guard's eyes could read as looking at Padmini as much as at Nagoji. The strapped staff has brass ferrules and is more polished than the gnarled stick on her sheet. There is no text, noose or gore. Lettering space: open sky across the top centre and right (about x 0.42 to 0.81, y 0 to 0.25). The guard balloons can go top right with tails down to the guard, and Padmini's long line above and right of her head.

Hard checks pass: Nagoji's ear is a tiny flush stud with nothing hanging, chin clean-shaven, boots on, sleeves down to the wrists, Padmini's hair thick and black, Kerala setting with plain unmarked banners, no text. Continuity problem for the author: the horses are swapped compared with 2.1 and page 1. There, Nagoji rides the black horse with the white blaze and Padmini the bay; here Nagoji dismounts from the bay and Padmini stands at the black horse. Minor: the verandah women wear stitched short-sleeved blouses, which are doubtful for 1740s Kerala. The clerk and the swordsman wear upper cloths instead of being bare-chested. Padmini's sword hilt sits at her left hip, not her right. Nagoji's mid-dismount pose is slightly awkward but reads. Both Padmini lines fit in the sky and on the roof at the upper centre and right.

Acceptable, with two small acting and prop differences. This is consistent with the script's sword. Hard checks pass: Padmini's hair is thick and black, coiled at the nape, with no grey. Her sari is cream with a gold border as on her sheet, and she has her walking stick. Revathi has her bare right shoulder, armlets, jasmine braid and sandalwood line. (3) Her necklace is round gold beads rather than flat coins, which matches her sheet but not the bible line. Lettering space: wall above her head and sky between the pillars at upper right.

Clean on every hard check: seated on a woven mat, Kerala stone verandah with a tiled-roof courtyard, no text, plain hair parting, indigo-and-gold sari over the LEFT shoulder with the RIGHT shoulder bare, coin necklace, armlets, anklet, jasmine braid and sandalwood line all present. Shows the beat: his right hand pushes the cream sleeve up past the elbow of the bared left forearm, palm up. The brand is a pale puckered ring of raised ridges about a hand's width above the wrist, with no letters, numerals or cross. The long thin white scar runs from the wrist toward the elbow. Red sash, mat, brass lamp, Kerala verandah, no text. Ear and chin are not in frame, and sleeves are exempt here. Minor: the gripping right forearm at the left edge shows bare skin with no sleeve visible (allowed, since 5.2 is exempt from the sleeve rule), and the ridged nails are hard to see. No face is drawn: put the NAGOJI (off) tail at the top-left edge and the REVATHI (off) tails at the right edge, toward where his arm reaches. Lettering space: the floor and mat in the lower middle, and the pillar and wall at upper right.

Hard checks pass. The ear ornament is a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging. The moustache is thick and curled. Sleeves are down to the wrists. He sits on the mat, and his feet are out of frame. Rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash and talwar hilt are correct. The memory bleeds in at the right edge like a stain: a clerk's hand with a quill over an open ledger in a stone cellar under a slit window, with only ruled columns and grey smudges, no letters or numerals. Kerala verandah, no text. Minor: light shadow-stubble texture on the chin and jaw; it still reads as clean-shaven. Minor: he looks toward frame right (into the memory), while Revathi in 5.1 and 5.3 also looks right, so the screen direction between them is loose. Lettering space: the sky and courtyard wall above the middle, and the stone pillar at upper left.

Hard checks pass: seated cross-legged on the woven mat, Kerala verandah and courtyard, no text, correct costume (sari over the LEFT shoulder, RIGHT shoulder bare, coin necklace, armlets, anklet, jasmine braid, sandalwood line). Her narrowed sidelong frown while eating reads as the beat, and the hands are sound. Minor prop drift: she eats a whole peeled banana, and a brass bowl of whole bananas with a brass pot sits beside her, where 5.3 showed a single piece of plantain and 5.1 the rice plate. Minor: the hair parting has a faint orange-brown tone, the same as the accepted page 4 frames and much fainter than the red streak rejected in 5.3. Lettering space: the plain wall at upper middle.

All hard checks pass. Nagoji has a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, a clean chin (only faint texture shading), sleeves to the wrists, bare feet and a mat. Revathi's right shoulder is bare and the sari end is over her left. No text, Kerala setting. Soft notes: (1) Screen direction is flipped against the rest of the scene. Revathi is at frame left and Nagoji at frame right here, but 4.4, 6.5 and 7.2 put Nagoji left and Revathi right. A mirror is not a fix, because it would move her bare shoulder to the wrong side. (2) The pointing finger is medium-sized rather than large in frame, and it touches the step edge in front of her own mat rather than exactly between the two mats. Lettering space: the low-detail red earth and stone step across the bottom, plus the sky and roof gap between the two heads at top centre.

Minor only: her right shoulder sits behind her braid rather than showing clearly bare, but there is no stitched blouse. Her upper back is bare skin and the pallu is over her left shoulder, so the fix holds. There is light hatching on Nagoji's jaw, but his chin still reads clean-shaven. The three balloons should stack in the top band (sky, pillar capitals, back roof, right wall), with the third over Nagoji's cream back if needed. Both heads stay clear.

Clean. Close on Revathi, seated on her mat. A band of shadow crosses her upper face, and she looks away from him with her chin on her hand. Passes the hard checks. Ear is a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging. Passes the hard checks. Nagoji's ear is a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, his chin is clean (faint stubble shading only), sleeves are down to the wrists and he is barefoot. All hard checks pass. v03 makes the required fix: Nagoji is small in a tall frame, barefoot on red earth, with the laterite gate behind him (left) and the lamp-lit hall ahead (right). The upper 40% is open sunset sky, with room for all four captions. Turban, cream tunic with sleeves down, red sash, talwar and clean chin all match the bible, and there is no painted text. Remaining fault, accepted for the author list: his ear jewel is a tiny gold bead hanging just below the lobe instead of a flush stud. It is about 3 px at full frame and barely visible at print size. Minor: a small framed rectangle (mirror or niche) on the wall deep inside the hall, too small to matter. v01 and v02 both draw Nagoji large in the foreground, which fails the 'small in a big frame' beat, and both have a visible hanging gold drop.

v03 is not picked because the region edit made things worse. The gold ball is still large and hangs below the lobe, and the edit box cut off the left curl of Nagoji's moustache, leaving a visible seam. v02 is a near-identical full re-render of v01 with no regressions (I checked faces, hands, feet and the elders side by side). Its near-ear jewel is a small gold bead sitting at the very tip of the lobe, and the far ear shows a flush stud. This is the closest of the three to a flush stud. Remaining fault, accepted for the author list: the near-ear bead sits a hair below the lobe edge, about 3 px at full frame. Pre-existing composition deviations, unchanged across all versions: Padmini stands in the lit doorway looking out toward Nagoji instead of talking with the elders, who are behind her inside. She also has a small red mark on her forehead that is not on her sheet, and carries a sheathed sword in her left hand. Clean chin, barefoot, sleeves down, night lamps, no text. The night sky top left and the dark pillar between Nagoji and the door can hold the caption and the servant's balloon.

Least flawed version, accepted with faults for the author. v03 did NOT make the fix. His torso faces the viewer, with the sash and left shoulder on the picture's right. The palm-out forearm on the picture's left carries the long white scar and the brand a hand's width above the wrist, so the marks are on his RIGHT inner forearm. His crossed left forearm carries a second scar and patch, so both arms are marked. v01 also puts the brand on his right forearm, near the elbow, and has a hanging ear drop. v02 is the only version with the branded forearm on his LEFT: his right hand grips his left forearm, and the sash and talwar are on the picture's right.
